cultural.vision_reason: This is a classic riga/boubou-style gown made of strip-woven cotton with metallic thread and embroidered "two knives" pocket motif — a garment type widely worn across the Western Sudanic/Sahelian region including Wolof communities of Senegal, consistent with the described construction and decoration.

physical.title: gown; tobe
physical.summary: Gown (tobe, boubou, riga), composed of 45 strips of hand-woven machine-made cotton, machine sewn together along the selvedges. The strips on the body are aligned vertically, but have been folded to taper towards the top, but are at full extent at the bottom; the sleeves flare out at the top. The strips are of uniform pattern, being warp-faced and made of buff coloured warps and wefts, with a band of gold metallic threads run through the middle of each strip. A large pocket has been sewn onto the breast, and this and the surrounding areas have been embroidered in the two knives (aska biyu) pattern in natural coloured cotton, with a large spiral on both the front and back of the tunic.
